title: [Q6] Decide virtual-table versus dedicated resumable graph cursor
description:
Measure worst-case work before first output, cancellation latency, fairness, and memory. Retain the virtual-table adapter or replace it with a dedicated yield-safe graph cursor/opcode based on evidence.

## Rationale

The existing virtual-table scan path minimizes core changes, but its synchronous cursor contract may not provide bounded cooperative execution for expensive shortest-path searches. The decision must be driven by measured latency and fairness.

## Alternatives Considered

1. Retain the internal virtual-table adapter when each call has bounded work and cancellation latency.
2. Add a dedicated resumable graph cursor/opcode when explicit yield-safe state is required.
3. Reject widening every internal virtual-table cursor to asynchronous I/O solely for graph traversal.
acceptance_criteria: Decision and measurements are recorded; chosen adapter passes cancellation/resource tests; any core state machine has deterministic yield, resume, and abandonment coverage.
close_reason: Measured and retained the internal GraphExpand virtual-table boundary with a specialized resumable cursor. A 256-operation quantum bounds state and raw-adjacency work; 100k-fanout gate runs had 0.547-0.625ms maximum calls, explicit yields, next-quantum cancellation, hard resource caps, exact resume, and safe abandonment. Validation: 55 graph tests, core vtab tests, strict graph/core Clippy, and 9,589 SQL tests plus turso-tests.

title: [D4] Decide and implement derived-state persistence mode
description:
Measure rebuild, startup, memory, write, and refresh costs; retain in-memory rebuild if sufficient, otherwise implement same-file versioned internal chunks with atomic publish. A sidecar requires a separate product decision.

## Rationale

CSR state is derived and must remain recoverable without weakening Turso's one-file or transaction guarantees. Persistence is justified only when measured rebuild and startup costs exceed the accepted envelope.

## Alternatives Considered

1. Explicit in-memory rebuild on demand.
2. Versioned opaque chunks or internal tables in the Turso file.
3. A derived sidecar only after an explicit change to the one-file product contract.
acceptance_criteria: Chosen mode is evidence-backed; crash/build/publish/stale/schema/corruption tests prove derived state is discardable and canonical rows remain unchanged.
notes: Decision implemented in e2ba3c4: retain InMemoryRebuildOnDemand for the experimental MVP. Reproducible snapshot_profile measured 1k/10k/100k sparse chains; 100k/99,999 rebuilt in ~0.54s, retained ~18.31 MiB, conservatively peaked ~27.47 MiB, startup was <0.003ms, and durable derived write amplification is zero. Snapshot status/metadata are observable; GraphExpand rejects stale catalog/generation state; sessions rebuild once per visible generation; explicit discard and process loss rebuild from canonical rows. Tests cover atomic replacement, stale publication, cancellation, resource failure, schema damage, discard/restart, canonical-row preservation, and rebuild. D5 dense/skewed/cyclic/high-degree benchmarks may reopen same-file chunks; sidecars remain excluded. Validation: 263 graph/Postgres crate tests, 367 turso_pg_tests, strict all-feature/all-target clippy, fmt and diff checks.
close_reason: Acceptance met by e2ba3c4: measured in-memory persistence mode has observable enforced freshness and deterministic discard/rebuild recovery without changing canonical rows.

title: Implement extend_graph_registration
description:
PR 1 of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-12-graph-catalog-host-api-design.md`.

Add `extend_graph_registration(connection, registration, polymorphic_roles) -> Result<RegisteredGraph, CatalogError>` next to `register_graph`.

- Graph must already exist (`GraphNotFound` otherwise). Do not create.
- Existing sources keep `SourceTableId` when table, identity, and roles match.
- New sources get the next id, role rows, type-registry row, and the same endpoint indexes `register_graph` creates.
- `SourceConflict` / `SourceRemoved` write nothing.
- Generation bumps iff at least one source was inserted.
- One savepoint.

Tests: add node+relation; idempotent second call; conflict; omitted source; missing graph; endpoint index once.

Do not change `register_graph` to extend on `GraphAlreadyExists`.

title: Implement replace_semantic_overlay
description:
PR 2 of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-12-graph-catalog-host-api-design.md`.

Add `replace_semantic_overlay(connection, graph_name, schema, fragments, constraints) -> Result<SemanticReplaceOutcome, SemanticCatalogError>`.

- Exact replay → `Unchanged`, no generation bump.
- Otherwise delete this graph’s semantic and constraint rows, insert the requested overlay, validate constraints, bump generation → `Replaced`.
- Do not drop graph sources or user tables.
- `register_semantic_schema_with_fragments` still returns `ConflictingSchema` on non-identical replay.

Tests: add a type over existing rows; unchanged replay; failing constraint rolls back; exact-register contract still fails closed.

Divergence tests stay in this crate. Do not export a host `DELETE` hook.

PR 3 of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-12-graph-catalog-host-api-design.md`.

- first install = `register_graph` + `register_semantic_schema_with_fragments`
- later sources = `extend_graph_registration`
